title: #hamlet #thepublictheater #shakespeare #shakespeareinthepark #central...
transcript: Last night my boyfriend Paul and I went to see The public's production of hamlet at the Delacour Theater in Central Park. Shakespeare in the park is a long standing annual tradition and an initiative of radical theater accessibility with every ticket being free. Although I've lived in New York for 5 years, this is actually the first time I attended Shakespeare in the park and it was a beautiful night. But I recommend preparing for various conditions and temperatures because this theater is very much outdoors. Producing and performing an almost 3 hour play outside, I'm sure, is quite a challenge, and I'm glad I knew the plot of hamlet before attending. There are just a lot of factors in the setting that could be distracting as an audience member, such as airplane noises, wind, and some guest starring raccoons off the edge of the stage. Nevertheless, the actors were always super present and this was definitely a full blown production. This was really interesting modern take on hamlet, although I thought some of the directorial choices were a little hit or miss and I don't think I really understood some of the political symbolism that was baked into it. I also felt it could have been abridged a bit more. But the performances were overall really great and this is definitely a production worth seeing, especially if you're a New Yorker looking to engage with the arts on a budget. With that, another playbill for my collection.
